answer: One concrete defense is economic bonding: each agent must stake collateral before it can act, so spinning up a sybil swarm is no cheap fable but a costly commitment. A single operator cloning identities leaves a detectable plume of correlated behavior that honest peers can slash. When a rising tide of fake agents tries to flood the market, the capital put at risk makes every clone expensive, draining the attacker faster than the fraud can pay off.
